issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Animal.name: the problem statement (lines 84-86 of problem_statement.md) explicitly requires the Animal.name attribute to use a StringBuilder to allow efficient in-place string manipulations. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the field as 'private String name;' (line 4). This difference between the specified internal type (StringBuilder) and the actual type (String) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the intended internal representation and how getters/setters should be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by changing the Animal.name field to a StringBuilder while preserving a simple external String API. Concretely: (1) change the field to 'private StringBuilder name;' (line where the field is declared); (2) in the constructor, initialize it with 'this.name = new StringBuilder(name);'; (3) implement public String getName() { return name.toString(); } so callers still get a String; (4) implement public void setName(String newName) { name.setLength(0); name.append(newName); } to mutate the existing StringBuilder; (5) review other classes (Seal, Pig, Goat, Farm) to ensure they use getName() and are unaffected. This preserves external behavior while satisfying the specification to use StringBuilder internally.
